text:
Josh Norris is a Sabre now, centring a lower line at about 14 minutes a night, and his season had felt stuck until last Thursday. He'd gone six games without a goal before scoring twice against Columbus, both times left alone in front for feeds from Zach Benson. The Buffalo News headline credited an "attack mindset".

Here's the case that it's about to get better. His own finishing is normal: four goals on 3.75 expected (the quality of his chances). The problem has been the people around him. With Norris on the ice, Buffalo has scored 11.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve, and that's cost him assists; he has one. His five-on-five numbers are solid (52% of the expected goals). Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.4 wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense. If the on-ice shooting just goes back to average, the points follow, and our projection has him somewhere around 40 by season's end. The health question that has followed him for years is the only thing that would change that.
